clue.text: Author looking exhausted and unwell

definitions.meaning: first meaning: H. Rider ..., the Victorian novelist of King Solomon's Mines
second meaning: gaunt and worn in appearance

explanation.surface: A writer who looks tired and ill, perhaps after a long deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A hints at a proper name: the author is H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a gaunt, drawn face, and the same word is the surname of a well-known adventure novelist.

clue.text: Astronomer in centre bowled over the Parisian

parts.note: a hub is a central point
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A stargazer at the centre of things is knocked flat by a man from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' looks like one phrase meaning stunned; split it, 'bowled' gives a letter and 'over' places it above the French article in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Hubble was the American scientist who showed the universe is expanding; the space telescope bears his name.

clue.text: Good army unit capturing a rocky height, a headland in Wales

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so the army unit surrounds the rocky height

parts.note: the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
a plus tor, a rocky hilltop on Dartmoor and elsewhere

explanation.surface: A capable regiment seizes a crag on a Welsh promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: The army unit is a four-letter corps abbreviation that opens in the middle to take in the height; tors are the granite outcrops of Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Orme is a limestone headland beside Llandudno on the north coast of Wales.

clue.text: An animal mounted in joint

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, something mounted is raised upwards, so the animal's name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A stuffed beast is put on display inside a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting the foot to the leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: County's best delicacy

parts.note: Devonshire is the full name of the English county of Devon; the possessive serves only the surface
the cream of something is its finest part

explanation.surface: A county boasting about its finest local speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England famous for its thick clotted cream served with scones.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream from the West Country is a prized treat, the heart of a cream tea.

clue.text: Stands by sponsor with drink

parts.note: to back a venture is to sponsor it
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Someone stays loyal to a patron over a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone loyally is to stand by them, both verb phrases in the third person.

clue.text: Dictator destroyed unionist's mobile

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked and broken up, so the following letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A tyrant smashes the phone belonging to a trade unionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussolini was the Fascist leader who ruled Italy as an absolute ruler from 1922 to 1943.

clue.text: Job-seeker is frank at end of tête-à-tête

parts.note: candid means honest and frank
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a phrase is its final letter, so only the last character is taken

parts.note: the closing letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: An applicant speaks openly at the close of a private interview.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is a person applying for a post, so someone seeking a job.

clue.text: Smart and carefully planned undercover operation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hurt with a sharp pain, as a verb
second meaning: a police set-up to catch criminals

explanation.surface: Praise for a clever, well-plotted covert police job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as an adjective praising the operation; it is the verb meaning to throb with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound can sting or smart; separately, a sting is a covert trap set by police or con artists.

clue.text: Carry on opening port

parts.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going and start something in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval and ferry harbour city in Devon, south-west England.

clue.text: Having equal cost and income in holiday flat

definitions.note: the answer is a verb phrase; the definition is a participle phrase describing the same state

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
an even surface is flat

explanation.surface: Renting an apartment for a vacation that pays its own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday flat' reads as one rented apartment; split it into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that breaks even has takings exactly matching outgoings, making neither profit nor loss.

clue.text: Loud? Piece for piano is, yes

indicators.note: a piece is a portion of something, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a composition for piano is loud, and hearing yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' in music means soft, which makes the surface clash nicely with 'Loud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisy makes a great deal of sound, which is what loud describes.

clue.text: Loose-limbed, Italian male after end of drill

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A supple Italian man follows the finish of an exercise drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the Italian man behind the drill's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful, moving with supple, easy limbs.

clue.text: Uneventful, a holiday not worth a postcard?

parts.words: a holiday not worth a postcard?
parts.note: surface reading: a trip so dull you send no card to family
setter's reading: the idiom for something unremarkable, taken literally as not worth a letter back to the family

explanation.surface: A dull vacation that does not merit sending a card to the folks.
explanation.walkthrough: The holiday picture turns the stock phrase literal: postcards are what you send home.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything ordinary and unremarkable, lacking interest or incident.

clue.text: See 12
Time to request to speak to Church of England working party

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ask for someone is to request a word with them
CE is the standard abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: It is time to request a meeting with the Anglican Church's committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group set up to deal with one specific job, just as a working party is.

clue.text: Extra run perhaps, may cause defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a run scored when a fielder's return throw goes past the stumps
second meaning: to topple or bring down

explanation.surface: In cricket, conceding a bonus run might lose the match.
explanation.walkthrough: An overthrow in cricket is a wild return by a fielder that lets the batsmen take extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a ruler or government is to defeat and remove them; in cricket it names a bonus run.

clue.text: Fruit crop — it's varied after start of August

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the month

indicators.note: varied means changed in form, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A late-summer harvest that differs from year to year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the anagram behind the first letter of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are small orange stone fruits, picked in summer, so a plural kind of fruit.

clue.text: Holiday-maker, one wanting R and R, we hear, after parking

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is matched by its pronunciation rather than spelling

parts.note: R and R is rest and recreation, so leisure; someone wanting it is a seeker

explanation.surface: A tourist parks up, looking for rest and relaxation.
explanation.walkthrough: The phonetic match works for the British pronunciation of leisure, rhyming with pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on holiday is out for enjoyment, a person chasing fun and amusement.

clue.text: An endless task for presenter

indicators.note: something endless has lost its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A never-finishing job assigned to a broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main host of a news programme, the person who presents it.

clue.text: Sofia cop nervous about onset of trial (by the very nature of the case)

definitions.text: by the very nature of the case

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters wrap the single letter
a nervous person is jittery and agitated, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Bulgarian policeman is anxious as his court case begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria; the bracketed definition is an unusually long gloss of a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, that is, as a direct consequence of the circumstances.

clue.text: Irishman entertaining daughter in saloon

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An Irishman treats his daughter to a drink in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Saloon looks like a pub, but here it is the British word for a closed family car, which Americans call a sedan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan is the American term for a closed four-door car, what British drivers call a saloon.

clue.text: Bar, stifling to staff

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother by enclosing, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub where the air is oppressive for the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees of the bar; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's, a type of staff.

clue.text: Live dance music

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to bop is to dance

explanation.surface: A concert of dance tunes played in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as the adjective about performance; it is the verb meaning exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex style of jazz developed in the 1940s.

clue.text: Discipline in class

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rank or category, as in biological taxonomy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a teacher keeping a classroom quiet; 'class' is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means good discipline and also a ranked group in a classification system.

clue.text: Enid cooked hot food over in capital

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the name's letters are mixed up

parts.note: the fodder

indicators.note: to turn something over flips it, so the pair before it runs backwards

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Enid made a hot meal in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: Ray in submarine at sea, not right one!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not means without, so the letters named after it are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shaft of light inside a submarine on the ocean, with the wrong one excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single ray of sunlight.

clue.text: Governing body of mine might

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, without the outer letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
might is strength or power

explanation.surface: A governing board might be one for a coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governing body' reads as one phrase about a board; split it, so 'Governing' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A party in power holds office and so is the one governing the country.
